title: Full-tier models (union-trained): production BNPL comparison and union holdout
caption: Full-tier models (3 union-trained packages: best_quality, 10 bag folds, 2 stack levels), scored from the models' minimum model set (the models the best ensemble depends on; prediction is identical to the full folder). Hurdles carry every head (ev / am25 / am50 / am75 / am80 / am85 / am90 / amstar); amstar tau* maximizes the Full model's own train R2 with its native argmax and is frozen (not refit on holdout or live). Top: last-3-month BNPL production cohort. Acceptance n=142,391 (census: every eligible user, no sampling error for this cohort). Delinquency n=2,997 (census: every eligible user, no sampling error for this cohort) (matured CaaS book of the last 180 days). The shaded bands and the "(95% CI)" figures treat each cohort as one draw from ongoing traffic (Wilson interval for the yes-share, delta method for past-due/principal, no finite-population correction). They show how far the rates could move on future traffic, not an error in this cohort's own numbers. Blue = stored autogluon_v25; rust = locally scored union Almost Full package 1 MSE (the shared baseline of every dashboard); charcoal = selected Full challenger. Bottom: union holdout, delinquency = 1 - pngi_rate.
note_html:
Top row (production, BNPL only): stored autogluon_v25 from pre_scored_users, the locally scored union Almost Full package 1 MSE on the same users (these two can differ), and the selected challenger. The cohort is every last-3-month BNPL bnpl.api_requests user with a stored v25: a census, not a sample, so the cohort's own rates carry no sampling error. Delinquency = the whole matured BNPL CaaS book of the last 180 days (every user with a matured installment, completed_plans > 0 and a stored v25): also a census.

The shaded bands and the "(95% CI)" figures treat each cohort as one draw from ongoing traffic (Wilson interval for the yes-share, delta method for past-due/principal, no finite-population correction). They show how far the rates could move on future traffic, not an error in this cohort's own numbers.

Bottom row (holdout): gated yes-share of union test_v25.csv (BNPL leftover + cards, same 80/20 split as prior v25). Delinquency = labeled unpaid share 1 − pngi_rate in the score tail — not Fritz CaaS pesos. The original Fritz Pages copy is unchanged.

Holdout users left out: 251 of the 2,133 holdout users have no geolocation_access value, so they cannot pass the geolocation gate. They are excluded from both holdout curves (the bottom row uses the other 1,882). The live top row follows the Fritz SQL instead: IFNULL(..., 0), a missing gate counts as a failure and the user stays in the denominator. Under that rule the baseline's holdout yes-share at 0.65 would be 37.4% instead of the 42.3% drawn. Each holdout variant states its own figures under the charts; the curves are not changed.

acceptance.sql: bnpl.api_requests last 90d INNER JOIN pre_scored_users autogluon_v25 IS NOT NULL

delinquency.sql: mothership_caas matured last 180d, completed_plans>0, autogluon_v25 IS NOT NULL
